comments.body:
CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S MECHANISM — the title and original description overstate what happens.

I wrote that 'every inbound DC ghost-identity mint fails silently'. That is WRONG. The mint is never
ATTEMPTED on the DC path, so nothing fails there today.

WHAT I MISSED: _ensure_inbound_assignee_identity (apply_inbound_records.py:50) guards on accountId:

    account_id = assignee.get('accountId')
    if not (isinstance(account_id, str) and account_id.strip()):
        return

and adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py:26-27 says plainly 'DC has no accountId at all'. DC user
objects carry name/key (REST v2), never accountId, and the function is called with the RAW Jira user
object (apply_inbound_records.py:155 and :321, both '_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity(
fields["assignee"], repo_root)'). So on a DC deployment the function returns at the guard and
ensure_identity_for is never reached.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE, and it is two separate things:

 1. THE ACTIVE GAP: DC inbound assignees never mint a ghost identity AT ALL — not because the mint
    fails, but because the guard requires an identifier DC never supplies. Cloud gets ghost identities
    on inbound; DC silently does not.

 2. THE LATENT LANDMINE: the ValueError is real and I proved it at the API —
      creation_channel='jira-datacenter' -> ValueError: invalid creation_channel 'jira-datacenter';
      must be one of ['cli','import','jira','mcp','python']
    It is simply unreachable while the accountId guard short-circuits first. It would fire the moment
    anyone extends the guard to accept DC's name — i.e. the moment someone fixes (1) without also
    fixing the channel. That is the trap worth documenting: the obvious one-line fix to (1) turns a
    silent no-op into a swallowed exception, which is strictly worse to diagnose.

So a COMPLETE fix is both halves together: teach the guard DC's 'name' as the external id when
accountId is absent, AND map the backend vendor to its family channel so the resulting mint validates.
Either alone leaves DC without identities.

The acceptance criteria as written still hold — 'an inbound apply under the DC backend MINTS a ghost
identity successfully, asserted by a test that FAILS against today's code' is satisfied by neither
half alone, which is the right bar. Only the stated mechanism was wrong.

HOW I CAUGHT IT: I was about to write the RED test and checked whether the DC path actually reaches
the failing call, rather than assuming my API-level repro implied reachability. It did not. A repro
that proves a function rejects an input says nothing about whether that input ever arrives.

comments.body:
FIXED AND VERIFIED — the repair rode story b4e3's commit, not a commit of its own.

WHERE THE FIX LIVES: commit 36e134401 ("b4e3: mint DC inbound identities as jira family"), on
origin/main and reachable from this worktree's HEAD (verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`).
Its message says so explicitly: "Folds in bug 5f48. Two defects that compound, so they land
together." Its trailer names `rebar-ticket: b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1` only, which is why this close
needs --force-close: no commit carries a 5f48 trailer, exactly as with 2bc7 earlier in this epic.

BOTH HALVES LANDED — the complete fix this ticket's correction comment demanded:
 1. THE ACTIVE GAP (guard) — `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` (apply_inbound_records.py:105) now
    reads `for key in ("accountId", "name")`, Cloud's key FIRST so Cloud behaviour is unchanged,
    falling back to DC's `name`. Previously it returned at an accountId-only guard, so DC minted
    nothing and nothing raised.
 2. THE LATENT LANDMINE (channel) — `_identity_provider_for` asks the BACKEND for its
    `identity_family` rather than using the per-deployment `vendor`, so the mint validates against
    the per-family vocabulary. The commit records why the family is DECLARED rather than derived:
    splitting the vendor on "-" fails OPEN (a future `import-foo` backend would collapse onto
    `import`, a real channel, and mis-stamp provenance silently), while a lookup table in the core
    reintroduces vendor literals that test_backend_neutrality forbids.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, each mapped to a test in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_identity_dc_inbound_heldout.py` — **9 passed in 5.78s** locally:
 * "an inbound apply under the DC backend mints a ghost identity successfully, asserted by a test
   that FAILS on today's code" -> `test_a_dc_shaped_assignee_mints_a_ghost_identity`.
 * "minted under the shared 'jira' provider/channel, matching the ticket path" ->
   `test_the_dc_identity_is_minted_under_the_SHARED_jira_provider`, plus
   `test_both_jira_backends_declare_the_shared_identity_family` pinning the declaration the design
   rests on.
 * "a test asserts the failure is not merely swallowed — the mint is observed to SUCCEED" ->
   `test_the_mint_is_observed_to_SUCCEED_not_merely_to_not_raise`. This is the criterion that
   matters most here, because the call site swallows every exception; "nothing raised" was true
   while nothing worked.
 * "CREATION_CHANNELS is UNCHANGED (no vocabulary fork, no migration)" ->
   `test_creation_channels_vocabulary_is_unchanged`; confirmed directly in source —
   `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py:160` still reads
   `frozenset({"cli", "mcp", "python", "jira", "import", "unknown"})`.

BEYOND THE STATED ACs, two tests guard the failure modes this ticket warned about:
 * `test_fixing_only_the_guard_would_swallow_a_channel_rejection` pins the HALF-FIXED state — it
   simulates accepting DC's name while leaving the vendor as the channel and asserts the swallowed
   exception's cause. That is what stops the two halves being split apart later, which was the
   correction comment's central worry: the obvious one-line fix to the guard alone turns a silent
   no-op into a swallowed exception, strictly harder to diagnose.
 * `test_cloud_accountid_path_is_unchanged` and
   `test_an_assignee_with_neither_identifier_still_mints_nothing` pin that the guard NARROWED
   rather than vanished.

WHY THIS GATES J11: recorded on [rebar:5200] as `depends_on`. J11 exists to prove data actually
moves; an inbound identity failure that converges and reports success is precisely the defect class
that would let J11 report success over broken behaviour. That dependency is now satisfied.

CLOSE CLASS: plan_defect. The DC inbound path was designed around Cloud's identifier and derived the
creation channel from the per-deployment vendor; neither was a regression and neither predated this
epic's work — the design itself did not account for a second deployment shape.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem (PROVEN, not inferred)

`apply_inbound_records.py` derives the inbound identity provider AND creation channel from the
configured backend's vendor string:

    vendor = select_backend(load_config()).vendor          # 'jira-datacenter' for DC
    rebar.ensure_identity_for(vendor, account_id, ..., creation_channel=vendor)

But the store vocabulary does not contain that value:

    CREATION_CHANNELS = frozenset({'cli', 'mcp', 'python', 'jira', 'import', 'unknown'})

Measured directly against a scratch repo:

    creation_channel='jira'            ext=acct-cloud -> returned '4802-2404-6de4-4167'
    creation_channel='jira-datacenter' ext=acct-dc    -> RAISED ValueError:
        invalid creation_channel 'jira-datacenter'; must be one of
        ['cli', 'import', 'jira', 'mcp', 'python']

(The failure only appears on a FRESH mint — an existing (provider, external_id) mapping is reused
idempotently and never reaches validation, which is why a naive probe shows a false pass.)

## Why it is SILENT — the part that makes this dangerous

The call is wrapped in:

    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply
        logger.debug('inbound: could not ensure identity for jira accountId %r', ...)

So on a Data Center deployment EVERY inbound ghost-identity mint fails, is swallowed, and is
reported only at DEBUG. The reconcile pass still converges and reports success. This is precisely
the failure mode epic e369's AC6 exists to catch: a swallowed exception can still converge, so
convergence is not evidence of correctness.

Consequence: DC inbound assignees never get identities minted, so assignee resolution degrades
silently on every DC pass.

## Why it is newly reachable

Before story J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1], `reconciler.backend` was validated as
`_as_choice(v, k, {'jira'})`, so config could NEVER select the DC backend and
`select_backend(load_config()).vendor` could never return 'jira-datacenter'. J7 widens that
choice set — which is what ACTIVATES this path. The defect is latent on main today and becomes
live the moment a DC deployment is configured.

## Also inconsistent WITHIN the same module

The ticket-creation path a few lines below already hard-codes the family channel:

    create_data['creation_channel'] = validate_creation_channel('jira')

So the ticket gets 'jira' while the identity path tries 'jira-datacenter'. One of the two is wrong;
per epic e369's shared-identity decision (DC-created tickets carry the SHARED 'jira' creation
channel and the deployment is distinguished by RemoteRef.instance, so nothing in the store
vocabulary forks per deployment), the ticket path is right and the identity path is the bug.

## Proposed fix (NOT to widen the vocabulary)

Map the backend vendor to its FAMILY channel at this call site, so both jira and jira-datacenter
mint under the shared 'jira' provider/channel. Adding 'jira-datacenter' to CREATION_CHANNELS is
the WRONG fix: it forks the store vocabulary per deployment, contradicting the epic's decision and
dragging in a migration + compatibility gate that the epic explicitly avoids. It would also
fragment identity across deployments (a Cloud and a DC identity for the same human).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] an inbound apply under the DC backend mints a ghost identity successfully, asserted by a test
      that FAILS on today's code
- [ ] the identity is minted under the shared 'jira' provider/channel, matching the ticket path
- [ ] a test asserts the failure is not merely swallowed — i.e. the mint is observed to SUCCEED,
      not that no exception escaped
- [ ] CREATION_CHANNELS is UNCHANGED (no per-deployment vocabulary fork, no migration)
compiled_state.title: DC inbound identity mint fails silently: 'jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel
